about: Power-support origin study. Robot frame mm: x forward, y left, z up (MuJoCo trunk_base). Print frame = robot frame + 57.5 mm in z.

history.claim: The integrated support was made on 2026-09-12 to replace the original power support (community a.obj = upstream power_support). It kept the battery in the original bay, put the large regulator under the battery and the small regulator between the hip servos, and replaced an earlier 69 mm rear backpack.
history.quote: 电池留在原电池区；大稳压器在电池下方，小稳压器在两台髋关节舵机之间。此前 69 mm 外伸背包已被本方案取代。

history.claim: The design note for that version is dated 2026-09-12.
Both regulators were moved into the torso so heavy power parts would not sit in the head.
history.quote: 两块稳压器移到躯干：大板放电池下方，小板放髋部之间。避免把较重的供电部件集中到头上。

history.claim: The large regulator was the Pololu D24V150F5 (servo 5 V); the small one the S13V30F5 (Pi, camera, amplifier 5 V).
history.quote: Pololu D24V150F5 提供舵机侧 5V，S13V30F5 提供 Pi、相机和功放侧 5V

history.claim: The lower deck and its two hanger posts are the "vented lower shelf for motor regulator" with the D24V150F5 screw pitch.
history.quote: # Vented lower shelf for motor regulator, exact screw pitch 25.4 X x 38.862 Y.

history.claim: The deck sits 13.43 mm below the original support and the rear end is 12.27 mm behind the original battery; width unchanged.
history.quote: 底端为 Z −57.5 mm，相对原支架低 13.43 mm。支架宽度仍为 54.50 mm。

history.claim: The 43.2 x 31.8 x 11 mm regulator had no collision-free spot inside the torso search box, which is why it went under the bay.
history.note: The empty candidate list is a fact; that it caused the under-bay shelf is inference from timing and the build-script comment.

history.claim: On 2026-10-09 the user rejected the central clamped battery and chose the original layout with the DFR1202 converter in the original battery location, powered from the wall charger over a tether.
history.quote: follow original layout and replace battery location with regulator/buck board.

history.claim: On 2026-10-09 the OpenRB-150 moved from the head onto the lower deck, held by a new printed tray.
history.quote: OpenRB-150 moves from the head to the power-support lower deck

history.claim: The current guide fits the support unchanged (10/1 print) and straps the tray to the deck with the four deck standoffs and two ties through the deck slots.
history.quote: drop it so the four round deck standoffs go into its four clearance holes

history.claim: The phase-1 walking runs removed the upstream power_support and NP-F970 collision geoms and added the integrated support as a visual only, so the simulator had no shin-to-support contact.
history.field: remove_meshes includes np_f970 and power_support; parts[0] power-support-integrated-body.stl added with contype=0, conaffinity=0 and no collision_box

history.claim: The phase-1 mass model kept the OpenRB (13 g) in the head, not on the deck.
The final phase-1 controller is kp 275, 20 ms action delay, prediction off; its 33 cases include one 40 ms sensor-delay case per mass.

The 2026-09-12 mesh check of the new torso parts against the legs sampled 250 of 1500 frames from kp 200 trajectories and found no overlap above 0.005 mm3. It did not cover the later kp 275 / kp 300 controllers.
history.field: sampled_frames, source_frames, cross_body_collisions; config kp in repair-final-perturb-batteryremove0-sensor40.config.json

history.claim: Upstream training (velocity task) penalises contact between the shin collision mesh and the upstream power_support collision mesh (weight -1.0); the upstream author expects the joint limits to keep the legs off the body.
history.field: rewards['self_collisions'] weight -1.0; geoms of class self_collision_only on mesh power_support and mesh leg
history.quote: discourages legs from crashing into the trunk battery holder
history.note: That the frozen walking policy was trained with this exact config is inference; the policy checkpoint does not record it.

regions.job_now: Mounts the torso to both hip-yaw motor cases and the torso base (M2 x 10 from below and above).

regions.region: battery bay: floor z -37.5..-36, top slab z 28..29.5, front posts, side lips (x -49.4..-21.8)
regions.job_now: Holds the DFR1202 converter insert on four sides (foam-taped to the bay floor); J and the 10 A main fuse sit in the open rear bay; the XT30 pigtail is tied to the support; the IMU holder rail sits 0.1 mm from the top slab.
Made for the two battery ties. No current guide step routes a tie through them (steps.py mentions ties only through the insert, the pigtail, the deck slots and the head hood).

regions.region: lower deck with four bosses and two vent/tie slots (x -59.1..-11.9, |y| <= 17.95, z -57.5..-53.5), 2878.5 mm3
regions.job_now: Carries the OpenRB tray (seated on the deck, 0.0 mm gap) via the four standoffs and two ties through the deck slots. The D24V150F5 it was made for is no longer in the build.
The only link between the deck and the rest of the part (without them the part splits into 15516.3 + 2878.5 mm3). This is where the shins touch.

regions.region: small regulator holder between the hip servos (x -20..9, z 3..32), 2113.3 mm3
regions.job_now: Empty. The S13V30F5 and its cover are retired; no current guide part overlaps the holder box (solids-report.json bounds).
